sentences.zh: 費宏，字子充，鉛山人。

translations.literal: Fei Hong, styled Zichong, was a native of Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Hong, courtesy name Zichong, came from Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 甫冠，舉成化二十三年進士第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: Just upon reaching manhood, he came out first in the metropolitan examination of the twenty-third year of Chenghua and was appointed an Academician-Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: Still in his teens, he placed first in the palace examination of Chenghua 23 and was made a Hanlin expositor.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，遷左贊善，直講東宮，進左諭德。

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi reign he was transferred to Left Assistant Companion to the Heir Apparent, lectured in the Eastern Palace, and advanced to Left Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi he rose to left assistant tutor to the heir apparent, lectured in the Eastern Palace, and was promoted to left preceptor.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，擢太常少卿，兼侍講讀。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor acceded, he was raised to Vice Minister of Ceremonies and concurrently served as Lecturer and Reader.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengde Emperor came to the throne, he was appointed vice minister of rites and also served as lecturer and reader at court.

sentences.zh: 預修《孝宗實錄》。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Veritable Records of the Hongzhi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 充日講官。

translations.literal: He served as a lecturer at the daily audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He served among the lecturers at the emperor's daily briefings.

sentences.zh: 正德二年拜禮部右侍郎，尋轉左。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites on the right; soon after he was transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 2 he was made vice minister of rites on the right, and soon moved to the left vice ministership.

sentences.zh: 五年進尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 帝耽於逸樂，早朝日講俱廢。

translations.literal: The emperor was addicted to leisure and pleasure; early audiences and daily lectures were both abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave himself to pleasure, and both morning court and daily lectures lapsed.

sentences.zh: 宏請勤政、務學、納諫，報聞。

translations.literal: Hong memorialized urging diligent government, devotion to study, and acceptance of remonstrance; the response merely acknowledged receipt.
translations.idiomatic: Hong urged diligent rule, serious study, and openness to remonstrance; the court merely noted that his memorial had been received.

sentences.zh: 魯府鄒平王子當潩當襲父爵，為弟當涼所奪且數年矣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu's son Dangyi of Zouping should have inherited his father's title, but it had been usurped by his younger brother Dangliang for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Dangyi, son of the Prince of Lu's Zouping domain, ought to have succeeded to his father's rank, but his younger brother Dangliang had seized it years before.

sentences.zh: 宏因當潩奏辨，據法正之。

translations.literal: Hong took up Dangyi's case in a memorial and corrected the matter according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Hong took up Dangyi's cause in a memorial and set the succession right under the law.

sentences.zh: 當涼怒，誣宏受賂，宏不為動。

translations.literal: Dangliang was enraged and falsely accused Hong of taking bribes; Hong was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Dangliang, furious, accused Hong of taking bribes, but Hong stood firm.

sentences.zh: 明年冬十二月，命宏兼文淵閣大學士參預機務。

translations.literal: The next year, in the twelfth month of winter, Hong was ordered concurrently to serve as Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and take part in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter, in the twelfth month, he was made grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion with a seat in policy deliberations.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子太保、武英殿大學士，進戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional titles Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall, and was advanced to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was named grand guardian of the heir apparent and grand secretary of the Wuying Hall, and promoted to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 幸臣錢寧陰黨宸濠，欲交歡宏，饋彩幣及他珍玩。

translations.literal: The favorite Qian Ning was secretly allied with Prince Ning Chenhao and wished to win Hong's friendship, presenting him with colored silks and other rare curios.
translations.idiomatic: The favorite Qian Ning was secretly in league with Prince Ning Zhu Chenhao and tried to win Hong over with brocades and other rare gifts.

sentences.zh: 拒卻之。

translations.literal: He refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Hong refused them.

sentences.zh: 寧慚且恚。

translations.literal: Ning was ashamed yet resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was shamed and furious.

sentences.zh: 宸濠謀復護衛、屯田，輦白金巨萬，遍賂朝貴，寧及兵部尚書陸完主之。

translations.literal: Chenhao plotted to recover his princely guard and military colonies and sent tens of thousands in silver by cart to bribe court dignitaries far and wide; Ning and Minister of War Lu Wan championed the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao sought to recover his princely guard and military estates and sent cartloads of silver worth tens of thousands to bribe officials throughout the court; Ning and the minister of war Lu Wan led the effort on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 宏從弟編修寀，其妻與濠妻，兄弟也，知之以告宏。

translations.literal: Hong's younger cousin, the expositor Cai, had a wife who was sister to Chenhao's wife; knowing this, he told Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's younger cousin, the Hanlin expositor Cai, was married to Chenhao's wife's sister; learning of the plot, he told Hong.

sentences.zh: 宏入朝，完迎問曰：「寧王求護衛，可復乎？

translations.literal: When Hong came to court, Wan met him and asked, "The Prince of Ning seeks to recover his guard — may it be restored?
translations.idiomatic: When Hong arrived at court, Wan met him and asked, "The Prince of Ning wants his guard back — can it be restored?

sentences.zh: 」宏曰：「不知當日革之者何故？

translations.literal: Hong said, "I do not know why it was abolished in the first place."
translations.idiomatic: Hong replied, "I do not know why it was taken away in the first place."

sentences.zh: 」完曰：「今恐不能不予。

translations.literal: Wan said, "I fear it cannot now be withheld."
translations.idiomatic: Wan said, "I fear we may not be able to refuse now."

sentences.zh: 」宏峻卻之。

translations.literal: Hong sternly rejected the idea.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sharply rejected the proposal.

sentences.zh: 及中官持奏至閣，宏極言不當予，詔卒予之。

translations.literal: When a eunuch brought the memorial to the Grand Secretariat, Hong spoke out forcefully that it should not be granted; the edict nevertheless granted it in the end.
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch brought the memorial to the Grand Secretariat, Hong argued forcefully that the guard must not be restored, but an edict granted it all the same.

sentences.zh: 於是宸濠與寧合，而恚宏。

translations.literal: Thus Chenhao and Ning joined forces and bore resentment against Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao and Ning then joined forces and turned their hatred on Hong.

sentences.zh: 寧數偵宏事無所得。

translations.literal: Ning repeatedly spied on Hong's affairs but found nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Ning repeatedly spied on Hong but found nothing to use against him.

sentences.zh: 以御史余珊嘗劾寀不當留翰林，即指為宏罪。

translations.literal: Because the censor Yu Shan had once impeached Cai as unfit to remain in the Hanlin, they pointed to this as Hong's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Because the censor Yu Shan had once impeached Cai as unfit to remain in the Hanlin, they made that Hong's offense.

sentences.zh: 中旨責陳狀，宏乞休。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript ordered him to explain; Hong requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript demanded an explanation; Hong asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 命並寀致仕。

translations.literal: An order was issued for both him and Cai to retire.
translations.idiomatic: An order went out for both Hong and Cai to leave office.

sentences.zh: 寧遣騎伺宏後，抵臨清，焚其舟，資裝盡毀。

translations.literal: Ning sent riders to watch Hong's trail; when he reached Linqing they burned his boat and all his baggage was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Ning sent horsemen to track Hong; when he reached Linqing they burned his boat and destroyed everything he carried.

sentences.zh: 宏歸，杜門謝客。

translations.literal: Hong returned home and shut his door to visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Hong went home and shut his door to callers.

sentences.zh: 宸濠復求與通，宏謝絕之，益怒。

translations.literal: Chenhao again sought contact; Hong declined, and Chenhao grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao again tried to open contact; Hong refused, and Chenhao grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 會宏族人與邑奸人李鎮等訟，宸濠陰令鎮賊宏。

translations.literal: It happened that Hong's clansmen were in litigation with local ruffians led by Li Zhen; Chenhao secretly had Zhen attack Hong.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong's kinsmen were in a lawsuit with local ruffians led by Li Zhen, Chenhao secretly incited Zhen to harm Hong.

sentences.zh: 鎮等遂據險作亂，率眾攻費氏。

translations.literal: Zhen and his men seized defensible ground and rebelled, leading a mob to attack the Fei clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and his followers seized strong positions and rose in revolt, leading a mob against the Fei family.

sentences.zh: 索宏不得，執所與訟者支解之，發宏先人冢，毀其家，劫掠遠近，眾至三千人。

translations.literal: Unable to seize Hong, they took the party to the lawsuit, dismembered him, opened Hong's ancestors' tombs, ruined his household, and plundered far and near until their numbers reached three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to seize Hong, they took his kinsman in the suit, dismembered him, opened the Fei ancestral tombs, wrecked the household, and plundered the countryside until their band numbered three thousand.

sentences.zh: 宏馳使訴於朝。

translations.literal: Hong sent a messenger in haste to lodge a complaint at court.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent a messenger posthaste to appeal to the court.

sentences.zh: 下巡撫孫燧按狀，始遣兵剿滅。

translations.literal: The case was referred to the grand coordinator Sun Sui for investigation, and troops were finally sent to suppress and destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the grand coordinator Sun Sui for investigation, and troops were finally sent to crush the rebels.

sentences.zh: 宸濠敗，言者爭請召宏。

translations.literal: When Chenhao was defeated, memorialists vied to request that Hong be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After Chenhao's defeat, memorialists vied to have Hong recalled.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遣行人即家起宏，加少保，入輔政。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor came to the throne, he sent an envoy to summon Hong from his home, gave him the additional title Junior Guardian, and brought him in to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor acceded, he sent an envoy to summon Hong from his home, gave him the rank of junior guardian, and brought him back into government.

sentences.zh: 宏持重識大體，明習國家故事。

translations.literal: Hong was steady and grasped the larger pattern, well versed in the precedents of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was grave and saw the larger pattern, thoroughly versed in state precedent.

sentences.zh: 與楊廷和、蔣冕、毛紀同心協贊，數勸帝革武宗弊政。

translations.literal: Together with Yang Tinghe, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji he worked in concert and repeatedly urged the emperor to reform the abuses of the Wuzong reign.
translations.idiomatic: With Yang Tinghe, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji he worked as one and repeatedly urged the emperor to undo the abuses of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 「大禮」之議，諸臣力與帝爭，帝不能堪。

translations.literal: In the controversy over the "Great Rites," the ministers strove with the emperor, who could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Great Rites controversy the ministers strove with the emperor until he could bear it no longer.

sentences.zh: 宏頗揣知帝旨，第署名公疏，未嘗特諫，以是帝心善之。

translations.literal: Hong had somewhat gauged the emperor's intent; he merely signed joint memorials and never remonstrated separately, for which reason the emperor favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had some sense of the emperor's mind; he only signed collective memorials and never remonstrated on his own, and for that the emperor looked on him kindly.

sentences.zh: 及廷和等去位，宏為首輔。

translations.literal: When Tinghe and the others left office, Hong became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Tinghe and the others left office, Hong became chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 加少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、謹身殿大學士，委任甚至。

translations.literal: He was given Junior Preceptor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall — trust in him was at its height.
translations.idiomatic: He was made junior preceptor, concurrently grand preceptor of the heir apparent, minister of personnel, and grand secretary of the Jinshen Hall; the trust placed in him was at its height.

sentences.zh: 戶部議督正德時逋賦，宏偕石缶、賈詠請斷自十年以後。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue proposed to press for arrears from the Zhengde era; Hong together with Shi Fu and Jia Yong requested that collection begin only from ten years onward.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue proposed to press for Zhengde tax arrears, Hong joined Shi Fu and Jia Yong in asking that collection be limited to the last ten years.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝以四方災異，敕群臣修省。

translations.literal: Because of calamities and anomalies in every quarter, the emperor ordered the ministers to examine themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When disasters and portents arose in every quarter, the emperor ordered the ministers to examine themselves.

sentences.zh: 宏等因言：「陛下用度無節，工役不休。

translations.literal: Hong and the others thereupon said: "Your Majesty's expenditures are without restraint and labor projects never cease.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and the others then said, "Your Majesty's spending knows no limit and public works never cease.

sentences.zh: 畿內土地半成莊田，內庫收納要求逾倍。

translations.literal: Within the capital region half the land has become estate fields, and the inner treasury's collections are demanded at more than double.
translations.idiomatic: Half the land in the capital region has been turned into estates, and demands on the inner treasury have more than doubled.

sentences.zh: 太倉無三年之積而冗食日增，京營無十萬之兵而赴工不已。

translations.literal: The Grand Canal granary has no three years' store yet superfluous consumption grows daily; the capital garrison has not a hundred thousand troops yet men are sent to labor without end.
translations.idiomatic: The Taicang granaries hold less than three years' grain while useless mouths grow daily; the capital garrison lacks a hundred thousand soldiers yet men are still sent to labor without end.

sentences.zh: 直臣得罪未見原，言官舉職乃被詰。

translations.literal: Upright ministers who offended have not been pardoned, while censors who performed their duty have been rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Straight-speaking ministers who fell afoul of the throne have not been forgiven, while censors who did their duty have been rebuked.

sentences.zh: 律所當行者數經讞不誅，罪無可辨者遽傳旨獲免。

translations.literal: Those who by law ought to be executed have repeatedly escaped death after trial, while those whose guilt could not be established have suddenly been freed by rescript.
translations.idiomatic: Men who by law ought to die have repeatedly escaped execution after trial, while others whose guilt was unclear have suddenly been freed by rescript.

sentences.zh: 幹和召怨，自非一端。

translations.literal: Offenses against harmony invite resentment — this is not the only cause.
translations.idiomatic: Such breaches of harmony invite resentment, and they are not the only ones.

sentences.zh: 」帝引咎褒答，然不能用也。

translations.literal: The emperor took blame upon himself in a gracious reply, yet could not put their advice into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the blame upon himself in a gracious reply, yet he could not act on their advice.

sentences.zh: 大同兵變，張璁請討之。

translations.literal: At Datong the troops mutinied; Zhang Cong requested a punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops mutinied at Datong, Zhang Cong asked that they be put down by force.

sentences.zh: 宏曰：「討而勝，玉石俱焚；

translations.literal: Hong said: "If we attack and win, jade and stone will burn together;
translations.idiomatic: Hong said, "If we attack and win, the innocent will perish with the guilty;

sentences.zh: 不勝，彼將據城守，損威重多矣。

translations.literal: if we do not win, they will hold the city and defend it, and our prestige will suffer greatly.
translations.idiomatic: if we fail, they will hold the city and our prestige will suffer far more.

sentences.zh: 莫若觀變而徐圖之。

translations.literal: Better to watch how matters develop and plan slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Better to watch how things unfold and move against them gradually."

sentences.zh: 」事果旋定。

translations.literal: The affair indeed settled soon after.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was indeed settled soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 宏為人和易，好推轂後進。

translations.literal: Hong was easy in manner and fond of advancing younger men.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was affable and liked to advance younger men.

sentences.zh: 其於「大禮」不能強諫，亦未嘗附離。

translations.literal: On the "Great Rites" he could not remonstrate forcefully, yet he never joined the opposition faction either.
translations.idiomatic: On the Great Rites he could not remonstrate forcefully, yet he never joined the opposing faction either.

sentences.zh: 而是時席書、張璁、桂萼用事。

translations.literal: But at this time Xi Shu, Zhang Cong, and Gui E were in power.
translations.idiomatic: But by then Xi Shu, Zhang Cong, and Gui E held sway at court.

sentences.zh: 書弟檢討春，故由他曹改用。

translations.literal: Shu's younger brother, the reviser Chun, had formerly been transferred in from another bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's younger brother Chun, a reviser, had earlier been transferred in from another office.

sentences.zh: 及《武宗實錄》成，宏議出為僉事，書由是憾宏。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Wuzong were completed, Hong proposed that Chun be sent out as an administration vice commissioner; Shu therefore resented Hong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of the Zhengde Emperor were completed, Hong proposed posting Chun out as an administration vice commissioner, and Shu bore a grudge from that day.

sentences.zh: 璁、萼由郎署入翰林，驟至詹事，舉朝惡其人。

translations.literal: Cong and E entered the Hanlin from the secretariat and were suddenly raised to Tutor of the Heir Apparent; the whole court detested them.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and E had entered the Hanlin from the secretariat and were suddenly made tutors to the heir apparent; the whole court detested them.

sentences.zh: 宏每示裁抑，璁、萼亦大怨。

translations.literal: Hong often showed restraint toward them, and Cong and E likewise bore great resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Hong often held them in check, and Cong and E hated him in return.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗禦平臺，特賜禦制七言一章，命輯倡和詩集，署其銜曰「內閣掌參機務輔導首臣」。

translations.literal: The emperor once held court on the terrace and specially bestowed a seven-character poem of his own composition, ordering a collection of responsive verses to be compiled and signing Hong's title as "chief minister of the Grand Secretariat who participates in state affairs and guides policy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once held court on the terrace, gave Hong a seven-character poem of his own composition, and ordered a collection of responsive verses compiled under the title "chief minister of the Grand Secretariat who participates in state affairs and guides policy."

sentences.zh: 其見尊禮，前此未有也。

translations.literal: Such honor had never been shown before.
translations.idiomatic: Such honor had never been shown to a minister before.

sentences.zh: 璁、萼滋害宏寵。

translations.literal: Cong and E grew still more envious of Hong's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and E grew still more jealous of Hong's favor.

sentences.zh: 萼言：「詩文小技，不足勞聖心，且使宏得馮寵靈，淩壓朝士。

translations.literal: E said: "Poetry and prose are minor arts, unworthy of the sage mind, and they allow Hong to ride on imperial favor and lord it over court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E said, "Poetry is a minor art and not worth the sage mind; it only lets Hong trade on imperial favor and lord it over the court.

sentences.zh: 」帝置不省。

translations.literal: The emperor paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 萼遂與璁毀宏於帝，言宏納郎中陳九川所盜天方貢玉，受尚書鄧璋賕謀起用，並及其居鄉事。

translations.literal: E then joined Cong in slandering Hong to the emperor, saying Hong had accepted jade tribute from the Western Regions stolen by the director Chen Jiuchuan, taken bribes from Minister Deng Zhang to secure appointments, and also attacking his conduct in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E then joined Zhang Cong in slandering Hong to the emperor, alleging that Hong had accepted Western tribute jade stolen by the director Chen Jiuchuan, taken bribes from Minister Deng Zhang to secure appointments, and attacking his conduct at home as well.

sentences.zh: 宏上書乞休，略曰：「萼、璁挾私怨臣屢矣。

translations.literal: Hong submitted a memorial requesting retirement, saying in summary: "E and Cong have repeatedly attacked me out of private resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Hong submitted a memorial asking to retire, writing in part, "Gui E and Zhang Cong have attacked me again and again out of private spite.

sentences.zh: 不與經筵講官則怨，不與修獻皇帝實錄則怨，不為兩京鄉試考官則怨，不為教習則又怨。

translations.literal: If I do not make them lecturers at the Classics Colloquium they resent it; if I do not put them on the Veritable Records of the Xian Emperor they resent it; if I do not make them examiners for the metropolitan and Nanjing provincial tests they resent it; if I do not make them instructors they resent it again.
translations.idiomatic: They resent me if I do not make them lecturers at the Classics Colloquium, if I do not put them on the Veritable Records of the Xian Emperor, if I do not make them provincial examiners in the two capitals, and if I do not make them instructors besides.

sentences.zh: 萼、璁疑內閣事屬臣操縱，抑知臣下采物望，上稟聖裁，非可專擅。

translations.literal: E and Cong suspect that I alone manipulate Grand Secretariat affairs, yet they should know that I merely gather public esteem below and report upward for the sage decision — this is not something one may monopolize.
translations.idiomatic: They suspect that I alone manipulate Grand Secretariat business, yet they should know that I only gather opinion below and report upward for the sage decision — that is not something one man may monopolize.

sentences.zh: 萼、璁日攘袂搤掔，覬覦臣位。

translations.literal: E and Cong daily roll up their sleeves and clench their fists, coveting my post.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day they roll up their sleeves and clench their fists, coveting my place.

sentences.zh: 臣安能與小人相齮龁？

translations.literal: How can your servant contend with petty men?
translations.idiomatic: How can I go on wrangling with such petty men?

sentences.zh: 祈賜骸骨。

translations.literal: I beg to be granted my old bones.
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to retire with my bones."

sentences.zh: 」不允。

translations.literal: The request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 及璁居兵部，宏欲用新寧伯譚綸掌奮武營，璁遂劾宏劫制府部。

translations.literal: When Cong took charge of the Ministry of War, Hong wished to appoint the Baron of Xinning, Tan Lun, to command the Exalted Martial Camp; Cong thereupon impeached Hong for coercing the ministries.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong became minister of war, Hong wished to put the Baron of Xinning, Tan Lun, in command of the Exalted Martial Camp; Cong then impeached Hong for coercing the ministries.

sentences.zh: 無何，又因宏子懋良坐罪下吏，攻之益力，復錄前後劾疏上之。

translations.literal: Before long, because Hong's son Maoliang was charged and sent to the magistrates, Cong attacked all the harder and again copied out his earlier impeachments and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when Hong's son Maoliang was charged and sent to the magistrates, Cong pressed his attack harder and submitted a compilation of his earlier impeachments.

sentences.zh: 不得請，則力求罷，詆宏尤切，章數上。

translations.literal: When his requests were not granted, he strove all the harder to be dismissed, vilifying Hong with especial bitterness and submitting memorial after memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When he was not allowed to leave office, he pressed all the harder to be dismissed, vilifying Hong with especial bitterness in memorial after memorial.

sentences.zh: 宏亦連疏乞休，帝輒下優詔慰留，然終不以譴璁、萼。

translations.literal: Hong also submitted memorial after memorial requesting retirement; the emperor repeatedly issued gracious edicts to comfort and retain him, yet in the end never rebuked Cong and E.
translations.idiomatic: Hong too submitted memorial after memorial asking to retire; the emperor repeatedly issued gracious edicts to keep him, yet never rebuked Cong and E.

sentences.zh: 於是奸人王邦奇承璁、萼指，上書汙故大學士廷和等，並誣宏。

translations.literal: Thereupon the villain Wang Bangqi, acting on Cong's and E's cue, submitted a memorial defaming the former grand secretary Tinghe and others, and also slandering Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Then the schemer Wang Bangqi, acting at Cong's and E's prompting, submitted a memorial defaming the former grand secretary Yang Tinghe and others, and slandering Hong as well.

sentences.zh: 宏竟致仕去。

translations.literal: Hong finally retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Hong finally left office altogether.

sentences.zh: 時六年二月也。

translations.literal: It was the second month of the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the second month of the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 十月，璁遂以尚書、大學士入直內閣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Cong entered the Grand Secretariat as minister and grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhang Cong entered the Grand Secretariat as minister and grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 間一歲萼亦入矣。

translations.literal: A year later E also entered.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Gui E entered as well.

sentences.zh: 十四年，萼既前死，璁亦去位，帝始追念宏。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year E had already died earlier and Cong had also left office; the emperor then began to recall Hong with fondness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Gui E had already died and Zhang Cong had left office; only then did the emperor begin to miss Hong.

sentences.zh: 四月，再遣行人即家起官如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he again sent an envoy to summon Hong from his home to office as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he again sent an envoy to summon Hong from his home to the same posts as before.

sentences.zh: 七月至京師。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the capital in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 使中使勞以上尊禦饌，面諭曰：「與卿別久，卿康健無恙，宜悉心輔導稱朕意。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a eunuch to comfort him with imperial fare and instructed him face to face: "We have been apart long; you are healthy and well — devote yourself to guiding me so that I am pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a eunuch to greet him with imperial fare and told him in person, "We have been apart a long time; you are hale and well — guide me with all your heart so that I am pleased.

sentences.zh: 」宏頓首謝。

translations.literal: " Hong bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 自是眷遇益厚。

translations.literal: From then on favor toward him grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the favor shown him grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 偕李時召入無逸殿，與周覽殿廬，從容笑語，移時始出。

translations.literal: Together with Li Shi he was summoned into the Hall of No Dissipation to tour the palace buildings, conversing at ease and laughing until a long while had passed before they came out.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Shi he was summoned into the Hall of No Dissipation to tour the palace buildings, talking and laughing at ease until a long while had passed before they emerged.

sentences.zh: 賜銀章曰「舊輔元臣」。

translations.literal: He was granted a silver seal reading "Former Chief Minister and Principal Subject."
translations.idiomatic: He was given a silver seal inscribed "Former Chief Minister and Principal Subject."

sentences.zh: 數有咨問，宏亦竭誠無隱。

translations.literal: The emperor often consulted him, and Hong also gave his utmost loyalty without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often sought his counsel, and Hong answered with complete loyalty and without reserve.

sentences.zh: 承璁、萼操切之後，易以寬和，朝士皆慕樂之。

translations.literal: After the harsh rule of Cong and E, he replaced it with leniency and harmony, and court officials all admired and delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: After the harsh rule of Zhang Cong and Gui E, he governed with leniency and harmony, and the court looked up to him with delight.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年六十有八。

translations.literal: Before long he died, at the age of sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 帝嗟悼，賻恤加等，贈太保，謚文憲。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in grief, doubled the funeral gifts and condolence payments, posthumously appointed him Grand Guardian, and gave him the posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, doubled the funeral gifts and condolence payments, posthumously made him grand guardian, and gave him the posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 宏三入內閣，佐兩朝殆十年。

translations.literal: Hong entered the Grand Secretariat three times and assisted two reigns for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Hong entered the Grand Secretariat three times and served two reigns for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 中遭讒構，訖以功名終。

translations.literal: Though slandered in between, he ended with honor and achievement intact.
translations.idiomatic: Though he suffered slander in between, he ended his career with honor intact.

sentences.zh: 其自少保入也，弟寀為贊善，從子懋中由進士及第為編修，宏長子懋賢方改庶吉士，父子兄弟並列禁近。

translations.literal: When he entered as junior guardian, his younger brother Cai was an assistant companion, his nephew Maozhong had passed the metropolitan examination with highest honors and become an expositor, and his eldest son Maoxian had just been made a Hanlin bachelor — father, sons, and brothers all held posts close to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned as junior guardian, his younger brother Cai was an assistant tutor, his nephew Maozhong had placed first in the metropolitan examination and become an expositor, and his eldest son Maoxian had just become a Hanlin bachelor — father, sons, and brothers all held posts close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 寀官至少保、禮部尚書，謚文通。

translations.literal: Cai rose to junior guardian and minister of rites, with the posthumous title Wentong.
translations.idiomatic: Cai rose to junior guardian and minister of rites, with the posthumous title Wentong.

sentences.zh: 懋中終湖廣提學副使。

translations.literal: Maozhong ended as vice commissioner for education in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong ended as vice commissioner for education in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 懋賢歷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: Maoxian rose to director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxian rose to director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 宏世父瑄，成化十一年進士。

translations.literal: Hong's clan elder father Xuan passed the metropolitan examination in the eleventh year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's clan elder father Xuan passed the metropolitan examination in Chenghua 11.

sentences.zh: 弘治時為兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi he served as a vice director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi he was a vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 貴州巡撫謝昶、總兵官吳經等奏爛土苗反，僭稱王，乞發大軍征討。

translations.literal: The Guizhou grand coordinator Xie Chang and regional commander Wu Jing and others memorialized that the Lantu Miao had rebelled and usurped the title of king, requesting that a great army be sent to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The Guizhou grand coordinator Xie Chang and regional commander Wu Jing memorialized that the Lantu Miao had rebelled and styled themselves kings, asking that a great army be sent against them.

sentences.zh: 以兵部尚書馬文升請，令瑄與御史鄧庠往按。

translations.literal: At the request of Minister of War Ma Wensheng, Xuan was ordered to go with the censor Deng Xiang to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: At the request of the minister of war Ma Wensheng, Xuan was sent with the censor Deng Xiang to investigate.

sentences.zh: 白苗無反狀，撫定之。

translations.literal: He reported that the Miao showed no sign of rebellion and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that the Miao had not rebelled and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 劾昶、經及鎮守中官張成罪。

translations.literal: He impeached Chang, Jing, and the eunuch defender Zhang Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Chang, Jing, and the eunuch defender Zhang Cheng.

sentences.zh: 遷貴州參議以終。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administration commissioner in Guizhou, where he ended his career.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administration commissioner in Guizhou, where he ended his career.

sentences.zh: 翟鑾，字仲鳴，其先諸城人。

translations.literal: Zhai Luan, styled Zhongming, was originally from Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Luan, courtesy name Zhongming, was originally from Zhucheng.

sentences.zh: 曾祖為錦衣衛校尉，因家京師。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather became a corporal in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and the family settled in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather became a corporal in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, and the family settled in the capital.

sentences.zh: 舉弘治十八年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi and was made a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Hongzhi 18 and was made a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 正德初，授編修。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he was appointed expositor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengde reign he was appointed expositor.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾改翰林於他曹，以鑾為刑部主事。

translations.literal: Liu Jin transferred the Hanlin to another bureau, and Luan was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin transferred the Hanlin to another bureau, and Luan was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 旋復官，進侍讀。

translations.literal: Soon his original post was restored and he was promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his original post was restored and he was promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，累遷禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of rites on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing he rose step by step to vice minister of rites on the right.

sentences.zh: 六年春，廷推閣臣。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year the court recommended grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year the court recommended candidates for the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝意在張孚敬，弗與。

translations.literal: The emperor had Zhang Fuxing in mind and did not appoint him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Zhang Fuxing in mind and passed him over.

sentences.zh: 命再推，乃及鑾。

translations.literal: He ordered another round of recommendations, and Luan was included.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered another round of recommendations, and Luan was included.

sentences.zh: 中貴人多譽鑾者，帝遂逾次用之。

translations.literal: Many eunuchs praised Luan, and the emperor thereupon appointed him out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Many eunuchs praised Luan, and the emperor appointed him out of turn.

sentences.zh: 楊一清以鑾望輕，請用吳一鵬、羅欽順。

translations.literal: Yang Yiqing, considering Luan's standing slight, requested that Wu Yipeng or Luo Qinshun be used instead.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing, thinking Luan too slight in standing, asked that Wu Yipeng or Luo Qinshun be appointed instead.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，命鑾以吏部左侍郎兼學士入直文淵閣。

translations.literal: The emperor would not agree and ordered Luan to enter the Wenyuan Pavilion as left vice minister of personnel with the rank of academician.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and ordered Luan to enter the Wenyuan Pavilion as left vice minister of personnel with the rank of academician.

sentences.zh: 尋賜銀章曰「清謹學士。」

translations.literal: Soon he was granted a silver seal reading "Pure and Diligent Scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given a silver seal inscribed "Pure and Diligent Scholar."

sentences.zh: 鑾初入閣，一清、謝遷輔政，既而孚敬與桂萼入，鑾皆謹事之。

translations.literal: When Luan first entered the Grand Secretariat, Yiqing and Xie Qian assisted in government; afterward Fuxing and Gui E entered, and Luan served them all with deference.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan first entered the Grand Secretariat, Yang Yiqing and Xie Qian were in charge; later Zhang Fuxing and Gui E entered, and Luan deferred to them all.

sentences.zh: 孚敬、萼皆以所賜銀章密封言事，鑾獨無所言。

translations.literal: Fuxing and E both used their granted silver seals to submit sealed memorials; Luan alone submitted nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxing and E both used their granted silver seals to submit sealed memorials; Luan alone submitted nothing.

sentences.zh: 詰之，則頓首謝曰：「陛下明聖，臣將順不暇，何獻替之有。

translations.literal: When questioned, he bowed his head and said: "Your Majesty is enlightened and sage; your servant can scarcely keep up with obedience — how could there be anything to remonstrate about?
translations.idiomatic: When questioned, he kowtowed and said, "Your Majesty is enlightened and sage; I can scarcely keep up with obedience — what could I have to remonstrate about?

sentences.zh: 」帝心愛之。

translations.literal: " The emperor came to love him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor came to favor him.

sentences.zh: 一清、萼、孚敬先後罷，鑾留獨秉政者兩月。

translations.literal: Yiqing, E, and Fuxing left office one after another; Luan alone held power for two months.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing, Gui E, and Zhang Fuxing left office one after another; Luan alone held power for two months.

sentences.zh: 其後李時、方獻夫入，位皆居鑾上，鑾亦無所怫。

translations.literal: Afterward Li Shi and Fang Xianfu entered, and both ranked above Luan, yet Luan showed no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Shi and Fang Xianfu entered, both ranking above Luan, yet he showed no resentment.

sentences.zh: 帝數召時、鑾入見，嘗問：「都察院擬籍谷大用貲產，當乎？

translations.literal: The emperor often summoned Shi and Luan for audiences and once asked: "The Censorate proposes to confiscate Gu Dayong's property — is that proper?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often summoned Shi and Luan and once asked, "The Censorate proposes to confiscate Gu Dayong's property — is that proper?

sentences.zh: 」時、鑾皆北人，與中貴合。

translations.literal: Shi and Luan were both northerners and sided with the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and Luan were both northerners and sided with the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 時曰：「所擬不中律。

translations.literal: Shi said: "The proposal does not accord with the law.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "The proposal does not accord with the law.

sentences.zh: 」鑾曰：「按律，籍沒止三條，謀反、叛逆及奸黨耳。

translations.literal: " Luan said: "According to the law, confiscation applies only to three cases: treason, rebellion, and factionalism.
translations.idiomatic: " Luan said, "By law, confiscation applies only in three cases: treason, rebellion, and factionalism.

sentences.zh: 不合三尺法，何以信天下。

translations.literal: If it does not accord with the three-foot code, how can the empire be made to believe it?
translations.idiomatic: If it does not accord with the code, how can the empire be made to trust the law?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「大用亂政先朝，正奸黨也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Dayong disturbed government in the previous reign — he is precisely a factionalist.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Dayong disturbed government in the previous reign — he is precisely a factionalist.

sentences.zh: 」鑾曰：「陛下，即天也。

translations.literal: " Luan said: "Your Majesty is Heaven itself.
translations.idiomatic: " Luan said, "Your Majesty is Heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 春生秋殺，何所不可。

translations.literal: Spring growth and autumn killing — what may not be done?
translations.idiomatic: Spring growth and autumn killing — what may Heaven not do?

sentences.zh: 」帝卒從重擬。

translations.literal: The emperor finally followed the heavier proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally followed the heavier proposal.

sentences.zh: 丁生母憂歸。

translations.literal: He went home on mourning for his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning for his birth mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，久不召。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was long not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was not summoned for a long time.

sentences.zh: 夏言、顧鼎臣居政府，鑾與謀召己。

translations.literal: Xia Yan and Gu Dingchen held the government; Luan plotted with them to have himself recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yan and Gu Dingchen were in power; Luan plotted with them to have himself recalled.

sentences.zh: 會帝將南巡，慮塞上有警，議遣重臣巡視，言等因薦鑾充行邊使。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to tour the south and feared alarms on the northern frontier, he discussed sending a high minister to inspect; Yan and the others thereupon recommended Luan to serve as frontier envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned a southern tour and feared trouble on the northern frontier, Yan and the others recommended Luan as frontier envoy.

sentences.zh: 十八年二月改兵部尚書兼右都御史，諸邊文武將吏鹹受節制。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighteenth year he was made minister of war and concurrently censor-in-chief on the right; civil and military officials of every border post were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighteenth year he was made minister of war and right censor-in-chief; civil and military officials on every frontier were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 且賫帑金五十萬犒邊軍，東西往返三萬餘里。

translations.literal: He was also given five hundred thousand in treasury silver to reward the border troops, and traveled east and west more than thirty thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given five hundred thousand in treasury silver to reward the border troops and traveled more than thirty thousand li east and west.

sentences.zh: 明年春入京，遂命以原官入閣。

translations.literal: The next spring he entered the capital, and was then ordered to re-enter the Grand Secretariat in his former capacity.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he entered the capital and was ordered back into the Grand Secretariat at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 在大同與總督毛伯溫議築五堡，過甘肅與總督劉天和議拓嘉峪關，皆受蔭敘。

translations.literal: At Datong he discussed with the grand coordinator Mao Bowen the building of five forts; passing through Gansu he discussed with the grand coordinator Liu Tianhe the expansion of Jiayu Pass — both received ennoblement for merit.
translations.idiomatic: At Datong he worked with the grand coordinator Mao Bowen on building five forts; in Gansu he worked with Liu Tianhe on expanding Jiayu Pass — both earned him ennoblement for merit.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，言罷，鑾為首輔。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Yan was dismissed and Luan became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Xia Yan was dismissed and Luan became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 時已加少保、武英殿大學士，進少傅、謹身殿。

translations.literal: By then he had already been made junior guardian and grand secretary of the Wuying Hall; he was advanced to junior preceptor of the Jinshen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had been made junior guardian and grand secretary of the Wuying Hall; he was advanced to junior preceptor of the Jinshen Hall.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩初入，鑾以資地居其上，權遠出嵩下，而嵩終惡鑾，不能容。

translations.literal: Yan Song had just entered; Luan outranked him in seniority and his power far exceeded Song's, yet Song ultimately hated Luan and could not tolerate him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song had just entered; Luan outranked him in seniority and his power far exceeded Song's, yet Song hated him and could not tolerate him.

sentences.zh: 御史趙大佑劾鑾私同年，吏部尚書許贊亦發鑾請屬私書，帝皆不問。

translations.literal: The censor Zhao Dayou impeached Luan for favoring a fellow provincial; Minister of Personnel Xu Zan also exposed private letters in which Luan solicited favors — the emperor inquired into neither.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Zhao Dayou impeached Luan for favoring a fellow provincial; the minister of personnel Xu Zan also exposed private letters in which Luan solicited favors — the emperor pursued neither.

sentences.zh: 會鑾子汝儉、汝孝與其師崔奇勛所親焦清同舉二十三年進士，嵩遂屬給事中王交、王堯日劾其有弊。

translations.literal: Then Luan's sons Rujian and Ruxiao, together with their teacher Cui Qixun's protégé Jiao Qing, all passed the metropolitan examination of the twenty-third year; Song thereupon had the supervising secretaries Wang Jiao and Wang Yaori impeach them for fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Then Luan's sons Rujian and Ruxiao, with their teacher Cui Qixun's protégé Jiao Qing, all passed the metropolitan examination of the twenty-third year; Song had the supervising secretaries Wang Jiao and Wang Yaori impeach them for fraud.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下吏部、都察院。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and referred the matter to the Ministry of Personnel and the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and referred the matter to the Ministry of Personnel and the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 鑾疏辨，引西苑入直自解。

translations.literal: Luan submitted a defense, citing his entry to duty in the Western Park as his excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Luan submitted a defense, citing his duty in the Western Park as his excuse.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，勒鑾父子、奇勛、清及分考官編修彭鳳、歐陽奐為民，而下主考少詹事江汝璧及鄉試主考諭德秦鳴夏、贊善浦應麒詔獄，並杖六十，褫其官。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier, stripped Luan and his sons, Qixun, Qing, and the sectional examiners the revisers Peng Feng and Ouyang Huan of office and made them commoners, and sent the chief examiner the junior mentor Jiang Rubi and the provincial chief examiners the preceptor Qin Mingxia and the companion Pu Yingqi to prison; all were beaten sixty strokes and deprived of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still angrier, stripped Luan, his sons, Qixun, Qing, and the sectional examiners Peng Feng and Ouyang Huan of office, sent the chief examiner Jiang Rubi and the provincial chief examiners Qin Mingxia and Pu Yingqi to prison, beat them all sixty strokes, and deprived them of office.

sentences.zh: 鑾初輔政，有修潔聲。

translations.literal: When Luan first assisted in government he had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan first entered government he had a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 中持服家居，至困頓不能自給。

translations.literal: Midway, while observing mourning at home, he was so impoverished he could not support himself.
translations.idiomatic: While observing mourning at home he was so poor he could not support himself.

sentences.zh: 其用行邊起也，諸邊文武大吏俱櫜郊迎，恒恐不得當鑾意，饋遺不貲。

translations.literal: When he was raised for the frontier mission, civil and military officials of every border post all met him in full armor beyond the suburbs, constantly fearing they might not please him, and presented gifts beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When he was sent on the frontier mission, civil and military officials on every border met him in full armor beyond the suburbs, fearing to displease him, and gave gifts beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 事竣，歸裝千輛，用以遺貴近，得再柄政，聲譽頓衰。

translations.literal: When the mission ended he returned with a thousand cartloads, using them to bribe those close to the throne, and thus regained power — his reputation collapsed at once.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission ended he returned with a thousand cartloads of gifts, used them to bribe those close to the throne, and thus regained power — his reputation collapsed at once.

sentences.zh: 又為其子所累，訖不復振。

translations.literal: He was also dragged down by his sons and never recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ruined by his sons and never recovered.

sentences.zh: 逾三年卒，年七十。

translations.literal: More than three years later he died, at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: More than three years later he died, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，復官，謚文懿。

translations.literal: When the Muzong Emperor came to the throne his offices were restored and he was given the posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Longqing Emperor came to the throne his offices were restored and he was given the posthumous title Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 李時，字宗易，任丘人。

translations.literal: Li Shi, styled Zongyi, was a native of Renqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, courtesy name Zongyi, came from Renqiu.

sentences.zh: 父棨，進士，萊州知府。

translations.literal: His father Qi was a metropolitan graduate and prefect of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi was a metropolitan graduate and served as prefect of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 時舉弘治十五年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Shi passed the metropolitan examination in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed expositor.
translations.idiomatic: Shi passed the metropolitan examination in Hongzhi 15, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed expositor.

sentences.zh: 正德中，歷侍讀、右諭德。

translations.literal: During Zhengde he rose through reader and right preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde he rose through reader and right preceptor.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，為講官，尋遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor succeeded, he was a lecturer and soon promoted to academician reader.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor succeeded, he was a lecturer and soon became academician reader.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing he was promoted to vice minister of rites on the right.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 3 he was promoted to vice minister of rites on the right.

sentences.zh: 俄以憂歸。

translations.literal: Soon he returned home on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went home on mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，為戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became vice minister of revenue on the right.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became vice minister of revenue on the right.

sentences.zh: 復改禮部，尋代方獻夫為尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred back to rites and soon replaced Fang Xianfu as minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred back to rites and soon replaced Fang Xianfu as minister.

sentences.zh: 帝既定尊親禮，慨然有狹小前人之誌，欲裁定舊章，成一朝制作。

translations.literal: After the emperor had settled the rites honoring his parents, he was moved to narrow the achievements of his predecessors and wished to fix old regulations and complete the institutions of his own reign.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor had settled the rites honoring his parents, he wished to surpass his predecessors and to fix old regulations and complete the institutions of his own reign.

sentences.zh: 張孚敬、夏言用事，鹹好更張。

translations.literal: Zhang Fuxing and Xia Yan were in power and both loved to change established practice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fuxing and Xia Yan were in power and both loved to change established practice.

sentences.zh: 所建諸典禮，鹹他人發端，而時傅會成之。

translations.literal: The ritual codes they established were all initiated by others, while Shi chimed in and completed them.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual codes they established were all initiated by others, while Shi chimed in and completed them.

sentences.zh: 或廷議不合，率具兩端，待帝自擇，終未嘗顯爭。

translations.literal: When court debate was divided he usually offered both sides and waited for the emperor to choose, and never openly contended.
translations.idiomatic: When court debate was divided he usually offered both sides and waited for the emperor to choose, and never openly contended.

sentences.zh: 以故帝愛其恭順。

translations.literal: For this reason the emperor loved his deference.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the emperor valued his deference.

sentences.zh: 四方上嘉瑞，輒拜疏請賀。

translations.literal: Whenever every quarter reported auspicious omens he would submit a memorial requesting congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the provinces reported auspicious omens he would submit a memorial requesting congratulations.

sentences.zh: 帝謙讓，時必再請。

translations.literal: The emperor would demur, and Shi would always ask again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would demur, and Shi would always ask again.

sentences.zh: 由是益以時為忠。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore regarded Shi as all the more loyal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore regarded Shi as all the more loyal.

sentences.zh: 賜銀章曰「忠敏安慎」，俾密封言事。

translations.literal: He was granted a silver seal reading "Loyal, Keen, Steady, and Careful," and permitted to submit sealed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a silver seal inscribed "Loyal, Keen, Steady, and Careful" and permitted to submit sealed memorials.

sentences.zh: 久而失之，請罪，帝再賜焉。

translations.literal: After a long while he lost it, requested punishment, and the emperor granted it again.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he lost it, asked to be punished, and the emperor granted it again.

sentences.zh: 十年七月，四郊成，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year, when the suburban sacrifices in all four quarters were completed, he was made grand guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the tenth year, when the suburban sacrifices in all four quarters were completed, he was made grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 雷震午門，彗星見東井，時請敕臣工修省，令言官指陳利害興革。

translations.literal: Lightning struck the Meridian Gate, a comet appeared at the Eastern Well, and Shi requested an edict ordering ministers to examine themselves and ordering censors to set forth what was harmful or beneficial and what should be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Lightning struck the Meridian Gate and a comet appeared at the Eastern Well; Shi asked for an edict ordering ministers to examine themselves and censors to set forth what should be reformed.

sentences.zh: 帝以建言乃科道專責，寢不行。

translations.literal: The emperor held that offering advice was the special duty of the supervising secretaries and censors, and shelved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that remonstrance was the special duty of the supervising secretaries and censors, and took no action.

sentences.zh: 光祿寺廚役王福、錦衣衛千戶陳昇請遷顯陵於天壽山，時等力陳不可。

translations.literal: The kitchen servant Wang Fu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the thousand-commander Chen Sheng of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard requested moving the Xianling mausoleum to Tianshou Mountain; Shi and others strongly argued that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The kitchen servant Wang Fu and the thousand-commander Chen Sheng asked to move the Xianling mausoleum to Tianshou Mountain; Shi and others strongly opposed it.

sentences.zh: 巡檢徐震奏於安陸建京師，時等駁其非制，遂議改州為承天府。

translations.literal: The inspector Xu Zhen memorialized establishing a capital at Anlu; Shi and others refuted this as contrary to regulation and thereupon discussed changing the prefecture to Chengtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector Xu Zhen proposed making Anlu a capital; Shi and others rejected this as irregular and the court instead made the prefecture Chengtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其秋，桂萼卒，命時兼文淵閣大學士入參機務。

translations.literal: That autumn Gui E died, and Shi was ordered concurrently to serve as grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and take part in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Gui E died, and Shi was ordered into the Wenyuan Pavilion as grand secretary with a seat in policy deliberations.

sentences.zh: 時張孚敬已罷，翟鑾獨相。

translations.literal: By then Zhang Fuxing had already been dismissed, and Zhai Luan alone was chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhang Fuxing had already left office, and Zhai Luan alone was chief minister.

sentences.zh: 時後入，以宮保官尊，反居鑾上。

translations.literal: Shi entered later; because his palace guardian rank was higher, he in fact ranked above Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi entered later, but because his palace guardian rank was higher he in fact ranked above Luan.

sentences.zh: 兩人皆謙遜，無齟齬。

translations.literal: Both men were deferential, and there was no friction between them.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were deferential, and there was no friction between them.

sentences.zh: 帝御無逸殿，召時坐講《無逸篇》，鑾講《豳風·七月》詩，武定侯郭勛及九卿翰林俱入侍。

translations.literal: The emperor held court in the Hall of No Dissipation, summoned Shi to lecture on the "No Dissipation" chapter, Luan to lecture on the "Seventh Month" poem from the Odes of Bin, and the Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun and the nine ministers and Hanlin all attended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held court in the Hall of No Dissipation, had Shi lecture on the "No Dissipation" chapter and Luan on the "Seventh Month" from the Odes of Bin, with the Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun and the nine ministers and Hanlin in attendance.

sentences.zh: 講畢，帝退禦豳風亭賜宴。

translations.literal: When the lecture ended the emperor withdrew to the Binwind Pavilion and bestowed a feast.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture ended the emperor withdrew to the Binwind Pavilion and gave a feast.

sentences.zh: 自是，數召見，諮謀政務。

translations.literal: From then on he summoned them often and consulted on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he summoned them often to consult on government affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年春，孚敬還內閣，事取獨裁，時不敢有所評議。

translations.literal: The next spring Fuxing returned to the Grand Secretariat and took sole decision in affairs; Shi did not dare to comment.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Fuxing returned to the Grand Secretariat and decided affairs on his own; Shi did not dare to comment.

sentences.zh: 未幾，方獻夫入，與時亦相得。

translations.literal: Before long Fang Xianfu entered, and he and Shi also got along.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fang Xianfu entered, and he and Shi also got along.

sentences.zh: 彗星復出，帝召見時等，諭以引咎修省之意，從容語及乏才。

translations.literal: A comet appeared again; the emperor summoned Shi and the others and instructed them in the idea of taking blame upon themselves and examining their conduct, speaking at ease also of the lack of talent.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared again the emperor summoned Shi and the others, spoke of taking blame and examining conduct, and mentioned the lack of talent.

sentences.zh: 時等退，條上務安靜、惜人才、慎刑獄三事，頗及「大禮」大獄廢斥諸臣。

translations.literal: When Shi and the others withdrew they submitted items on seeking tranquility, cherishing talent, and being cautious in punishments, touching somewhat on the ministers banished in the Great Rites cases and the great prosecutions.
translations.idiomatic: When they withdrew Shi and the others submitted items on seeking tranquility, cherishing talent, and being cautious in punishments, touching on ministers banished in the Great Rites cases and great prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔褒答之，然卒不能用也。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict in praise, yet in the end could not put their advice into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict in praise, yet in the end could not act on their advice.

sentences.zh: 給事中魏良弼、御史馮恩先後劾吏部尚書汪鋐，觸帝怒，時皆為論救。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Wei Liangbi and the censor Feng En successively impeached Minister of Personnel Wang Zhen, provoking the emperor's anger; Shi argued in defense of both.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Wei Liangbi and the censor Feng En impeached the minister of personnel Wang Zhen, provoking the emperor's anger; Shi argued in defense of both.

sentences.zh: 十二年，孚敬復入，鑾以憂去，獻夫致仕。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Fuxing entered again; Luan left on mourning and Xianfu retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Fuxing returned; Luan left on mourning and Xianfu retired.

sentences.zh: 時隨孚敬後，拱手唯諾而已，以故孚敬安之。

translations.literal: Shi followed after Fuxing, bowing with hands clasped and assenting to everything, and for this reason Fuxing was at ease with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi followed after Fuxing, bowing with clasped hands and assenting to everything, and Fuxing was at ease with him.

sentences.zh: 孚敬謝政，費宏再入，未幾卒，時遂獨相。

translations.literal: When Fuxing left office Fei Hong entered again; before long he died, and Shi then served alone as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuxing left office Fei Hong returned; before long Hong died, and Shi then served alone as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 時素寬平，至是益鎮以安靜。

translations.literal: Shi had always been lenient and fair; at this point he governed all the more with quiet restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Shi had always been lenient and fair; now he governed all the more with quiet restraint.

sentences.zh: 帝亦恒召對便殿，接膝咨詢。

translations.literal: The emperor also often summoned him for audiences in the side hall and consulted him knee to knee.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also often summoned him to the side hall and consulted him knee to knee.

sentences.zh: 時雖無大匡救，而議論恒本忠厚，廷論鹹以時為賢。

translations.literal: Though Shi had no great rescue of the state, his discourse was always rooted in loyalty and generosity, and court opinion all regarded him as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Though he effected no great rescue of the state, his discourse was always rooted in loyalty and generosity, and the court regarded him as worthy.

sentences.zh: 客星見天棓旁，帝問所主事應。

translations.literal: A guest star appeared beside the Celestial Lance; the emperor asked what event it foretold.
translations.idiomatic: A guest star appeared beside the Celestial Lance; the emperor asked what it foretold.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「事應之說起漢京房，未必皆合。

translations.literal: He replied: "The theory of events foretold arose with Jing Fang of Han and does not necessarily always fit.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The theory of events foretold arose with Jing Fang of Han and does not necessarily always fit.

sentences.zh: 惟在人君修德以弭之。

translations.literal: Only if the ruler cultivates virtue may it be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Only if the ruler cultivates virtue may it be stilled."

sentences.zh: 」帝稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this.

sentences.zh: 扈蹕謁陵，道沙河，帝見居民蕭索，愴然曰：「七陵在此，宜加守護。

translations.literal: Accompanying the imperial procession to visit the tombs, on the road at Shahe the emperor saw the inhabitants desolate and said with distress: "The seven tombs are here — they ought to receive added protection.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the imperial procession to the tombs, on the road at Shahe the emperor saw the inhabitants desolate and said with distress, "The seven tombs are here — they ought to receive added protection.

sentences.zh: 」時對曰：「昔邱濬建議，京師當設四輔，以臨清為南，昌平為北，薊州、保定為東西，各屯兵一二萬。

translations.literal: " Shi replied: "Formerly Qiu Jun proposed that the capital ought to have four auxiliaries, taking Linqing as south, Changping as north, and Jizhou and Baoding as east and west, each garrisoning ten or twenty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi replied, "Formerly Qiu Jun proposed four auxiliaries for the capital — Linqing to the south, Changping to the north, Jizhou and Baoding to east and west — each garrisoning ten or twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 今若於昌平增一總兵，可南衛京師，北護陵寢。

translations.literal: If now a regional commander were added at Changping, he could guard the capital to the south and protect the tombs to the north.
translations.idiomatic: If a regional commander were added at Changping, he could guard the capital to the south and the tombs to the north."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃下廷臣勘議，於沙河築鞏華城，為置戍焉。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon ordered the court to investigate and discuss, and at Shahe the Gonghua walled city was built and a garrison established.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the court to investigate, and at Shahe the Gonghua walled city was built with a garrison.

sentences.zh: 屢加少傅、太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly made junior preceptor, grand preceptor of the heir apparent, minister of personnel, and grand secretary of the Huagai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly made junior preceptor, grand preceptor of the heir apparent, minister of personnel, and grand secretary of the Huagai Hall.

sentences.zh: 會夏言入輔，時不與抗，每事推讓言，言亦安之。

translations.literal: When Xia Yan entered to assist, Shi did not contend with him but yielded the lead in every matter, and Yan was also at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Yan entered to assist, Shi did not contend with him but yielded in every matter, and Yan was at ease.

sentences.zh: 帝待時不如孚敬、言，然少責辱，始終不替。

translations.literal: The emperor did not treat Shi as he did Fuxing and Yan, yet seldom rebuked or humiliated him, and he was never removed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not treat Shi as he did Fuxing and Yan, yet seldom rebuked him, and he was never removed.

sentences.zh: 孚敬、言亦不敢望也。

translations.literal: Fuxing and Yan also did not dare to expect such treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxing and Yan also did not dare to expect such treatment.

sentences.zh: 十七年十二月卒官，贈太傅，謚文康。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventeenth year he died in office; he was posthumously made grand preceptor with the title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the seventeenth year he died in office; he was posthumously made grand preceptor with the title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 顧鼎臣，字九和，昆山人。

translations.literal: Gu Dingchen, styled Jiuhe, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Dingchen, courtesy name Jiuhe, came from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年進士第一。

translations.literal: He came out first in the metropolitan examination of the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the metropolitan examination of Hongzhi 18.

sentences.zh: 授修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed expositor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed expositor.

sentences.zh: 正德初，再遷左諭德。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he was twice promoted to left preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhengde he was twice promoted to left preceptor.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，直經筵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he lectured at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jiajing he lectured at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 進講範浚《心箴》，敷陳剴切。

translations.literal: He lectured on Fan Jun's "Maxims of the Mind," setting forth the argument with force and clarity.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on Fan Jun's Maxims of the Mind with force and clarity.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，乃自為註釋，而鼎臣特受眷。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and himself wrote a commentary, and Dingchen received special favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, wrote a commentary himself, and Dingchen received special favor.

sentences.zh: 累官詹事。

translations.literal: He rose to tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉世揚、李仁劾鼎臣汙佞。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Liu Shiyang and Li Ren impeached Dingchen as corrupt and fawning.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries Liu Shiyang and Li Ren impeached Dingchen as corrupt and fawning.

sentences.zh: 帝下世揚等獄，以鼎臣救，得薄譴。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Shiyang and the others to prison; because Dingchen interceded they received only light punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Shiyang and the others to prison; because Dingchen interceded they received only light punishment.

sentences.zh: 拜禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice minister of rites on the right.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of rites on the right.

sentences.zh: 帝好長生術，內殿設齋醮。

translations.literal: The emperor loved the arts of longevity and set up fasting and offerings in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved the arts of longevity and set up fasting and offerings in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣進《步虛詞》七章，且列上壇中應行事。

translations.literal: Dingchen presented seven stanzas of "Pacing the Void" and also listed what ought to be done on the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen presented seven stanzas of Pacing the Void and listed what ought to be done on the altar.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔褒答，悉從之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict in praise and followed all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict in praise and followed all of it.

sentences.zh: 詞臣以青詞結主知，由鼎臣倡也。

translations.literal: It was from Dingchen that the literary officials began winning the sovereign's favor with green prose.
translations.idiomatic: It was from Dingchen that literary officials began winning the sovereign's favor with green prose.

sentences.zh: 改吏部左侍郎，掌詹事府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left vice minister of personnel and directed the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left vice minister of personnel and directed the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 請令曾子後授《五經》博士，比三氏子孫，從之。

translations.literal: He requested that descendants of Zengzi be appointed doctors of the Five Classics, on the model of the three sages' descendants, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that descendants of Zengzi be appointed doctors of the Five Classics, on the model of the three sages' descendants, and this was granted.

sentences.zh: 大同軍變，張孚敬主用兵，鼎臣言不可，帝嘉納。

translations.literal: When the Datong garrison mutinied Zhang Fuxing advocated using troops; Dingchen said this could not be done, and the emperor praised and accepted his view.
translations.idiomatic: When the Datong garrison mutinied Zhang Fuxing advocated using troops; Dingchen opposed it, and the emperor praised and accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 十三年孟冬，享廟，命鼎臣及侍郎霍韜捧主。

translations.literal: In the first winter month of the thirteenth year, at the temple sacrifice, Dingchen and Vice Minister Huo Tao were ordered to carry the spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: In the first winter month of the thirteenth year, at the temple sacrifice, Dingchen and Vice Minister Huo Tao were ordered to carry the spirit tablets.

sentences.zh: 二人有期功服，當辭。

translations.literal: Both were in mourning for relatives within one year and ought to have declined.
translations.idiomatic: Both were in mourning for relatives within one year and ought to have declined.

sentences.zh: 乃上言：「古禮，諸侯絕期。

translations.literal: They thereupon submitted: "In ancient rites, feudal lords did not observe mourning for relatives within one year.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted, "In ancient rites feudal lords did not observe mourning for relatives within one year.

sentences.zh: 今公卿即古諸侯，請得毋避。

translations.literal: Present-day grand secretaries are the ancient feudal lords — we ask to be excused from declining.
translations.idiomatic: Present-day grand secretaries are the ancient feudal lords — we ask not to be excused."

sentences.zh: 」禮部尚書夏言極詆其非，乃已。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Xia Yan fiercely denounced this as wrong, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of rites Xia Yan fiercely denounced this as wrong, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 尋進禮部尚書，仍掌府事。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to minister of rites while still directing the household.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to minister of rites while still directing the household.

sentences.zh: 京師淫雨，四方多水災，鼎臣請振饑弭盜，報可。

translations.literal: In the capital there was incessant rain and floods in every quarter; Dingchen requested relief for famine and suppression of banditry, and the response was approval.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital there was incessant rain and floods in every quarter; Dingchen requested relief and suppression of banditry, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 十七年八月，以本官兼文淵閣大學士入參機務。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year he entered the Wenyuan Pavilion as minister with a seat in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year he entered the Wenyuan Pavilion as minister with a seat in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋加少保、太子太傅、進武英殿。

translations.literal: Soon he was made junior guardian and grand preceptor of the heir apparent and advanced to the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made junior guardian and grand preceptor of the heir apparent and advanced to the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，李時為首輔，夏言次之，鼎臣又次之。

translations.literal: At first Li Shi was chief minister, Xia Yan second, and Dingchen third.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Shi was chief minister, Xia Yan second, and Dingchen third.

sentences.zh: 時卒，言當國專甚，鼎臣素柔媚，不能有為，充位而已。

translations.literal: When Shi died Yan dominated government entirely; Dingchen had always been soft and fawning and could accomplish nothing, merely filling a seat.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi died Yan dominated government entirely; Dingchen had always been soft and fawning and accomplished nothing, merely filling a seat.

sentences.zh: 帝將南巡，立皇太子，命言扈行，鼎臣輔太子監國。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to tour the south and install the crown prince, he ordered Yan to accompany him and Dingchen to assist the prince in overseeing the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned a southern tour and installed the crown prince, he ordered Yan to accompany him and Dingchen to assist the prince in overseeing the state.

sentences.zh: 御史蕭祥曜劾吏部侍郎張潮受鼎臣屬，調刑部主事陸昆為吏部。

translations.literal: The censor Xiao Xiangyao impeached Vice Minister of Personnel Zhang Chao for accepting Dingchen's solicitation and transferring the principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments Lu Kun to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Xiao Xiangyao impeached Vice Minister Zhang Chao for accepting Dingchen's solicitation and transferring the principal clerk Lu Kun from Punishments to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 潮言：「兵部主事馬承學恃鼎臣有聯，自詭必得銓曹，臣故抑承學而用昆。

translations.literal: Chao said: "The principal clerk in the Ministry of War Ma Chengxue, relying on his connection with Dingchen, boasted he would certainly obtain a post in the personnel bureau, and I therefore suppressed Chengxue and used Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Chao said, "The principal clerk Ma Chengxue, relying on his connection with Dingchen, boasted he would obtain a personnel post, and I suppressed Chengxue and used Kun instead.

sentences.zh: 」帝下承學詔獄，鼎臣不問。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent Chengxue to prison and did not inquire into Dingchen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent Chengxue to prison and did not inquire into Dingchen.

sentences.zh: 十九年十月卒官，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the nineteenth year he died in office at the age of sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the nineteenth year he died in office at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚文康。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made grand guardian with the title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand guardian with the title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣官侍從時，憫東南賦役失均，屢陳其弊，帝為飭撫按。

translations.literal: When Dingchen served in attendance he pitied the uneven levies in the southeast and repeatedly set forth their abuses; the emperor ordered the grand coordinators to rectify them.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingchen served in attendance he pitied uneven levies in the southeast and repeatedly set forth their abuses; the emperor ordered grand coordinators to rectify them.

sentences.zh: 巡撫歐陽鐸厘定之。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator Ouyang Duo put them in order.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinator Ouyang Duo put them in order.

sentences.zh: 昆山無城，言於當事為築城。

translations.literal: Kunshan had no city wall; he spoke to those in charge and a wall was built.
translations.idiomatic: Kunshan had no city wall; he spoke to those in charge and a wall was built.

sentences.zh: 後倭亂起，昆山獲全，鄉人立祠祀焉。

translations.literal: Later when the Japanese raids broke out Kunshan was preserved whole, and the townspeople erected a shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Japanese raids broke out Kunshan was preserved, and the townspeople erected a shrine to him.

sentences.zh: 嚴訥，字敏卿，常熟人。

translations.literal: Yan Ne, styled Minqing, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ne, courtesy name Minqing, came from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試，以主司試錄觸忌，一榜皆不得會試。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination, but because the chief examiner's trial record offended someone, the entire list was barred from the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination, but because the chief examiner's trial record offended someone, the entire list was barred from the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十年成進士，改庶吉士，授編修，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jiajing he became a metropolitan graduate, was made a Hanlin bachelor, appointed expositor, and promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 20 he became a metropolitan graduate, was made a Hanlin bachelor, appointed expositor, and promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 三吳數中倭患，歲復大祲，民死徙幾半，有司征斂益急。

translations.literal: The three Wu regions were repeatedly struck by Japanese raids, and that year there was again a great famine; nearly half the people died or fled, while the authorities pressed collection all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: The three Wu regions were repeatedly struck by Japanese raids, and that year famine struck again; nearly half the people died or fled while the authorities pressed collection all the harder.

sentences.zh: 訥疏陳民困，請蠲貸。

translations.literal: Ne memorialized setting forth the people's distress and requesting exemption and loans.
translations.idiomatic: Ne memorialized the people's distress and requested exemption and loans.

sentences.zh: 帝得疏感動，報如其請。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved on reading the memorial and approved as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved on reading the memorial and approved as requested.

sentences.zh: 尋與李春芳入直西苑。

translations.literal: Soon he entered the Western Park on duty together with Li Chunfang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered the Western Park on duty together with Li Chunfang.

sentences.zh: 撰青詞，超授翰林學士。

translations.literal: He composed green prose and was abruptly appointed Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He composed green prose and was abruptly appointed Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 歷太常少卿，禮部左、右侍郎，改吏部，皆兼學士，仍直西苑。

translations.literal: He rose through vice minister of ceremonies, left and right vice minister of rites, and was transferred to personnel — all concurrently academician while still serving in the Western Park.
